children.translated_text: Now, the rites that are learned from customary practice.
They are to be performed during the northward course of the sun, in the bright fortnight, on auspicious days.
By one wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder.
In a clockwise direction.
The beginning is from the east or from the north.
And the conclusion is likewise.
In the dark fortnight are the rites belonging to the ancestors.
By one wearing the sacred thread in the prācīnāvīta manner, over the right shoulder.
Counterclockwise.
The conclusion is toward the south.
Occasional rites are those that depend upon a particular occasion.

children.text: agnim iddhvā prāgagrair darbhair agniṃ paristṛṇāti ||
children.translated_text: Having kindled the fire, he strews the fire around with darbha grasses whose tips point east.
Or with their tips pointing east and north.
In rites for the ancestors, with the tips pointing south.
Or with the tips pointing south and east.

children.text: uttareṇāgniṃ darbhān saṃstīrya dvandvaṃ nyañci pātrāṇi prayunakti devasaṃyuktāni ||
children.translated_text: Having spread darbha grasses north of the fire, he sets out the vessels connected with the gods in pairs, turned downward.
Those connected with human beings only once.
Those connected with the ancestors one by one.

children.text: pavitrayoḥ saṃskāra āyāmataḥ parīmāṇaṃ prokṣaṇīsaṃskāraḥ pātraprokṣa iti darśapūrṇamāsavat tūṣṇīm ||
children.translated_text: The preparation of the two pavitras, their measurement by length, the preparation of the sprinkling water, and the sprinkling of the vessels are as in the new- and full-moon sacrifice, but silently.

children.text: apareṇāgniṃ pavitrāntarhite pātre 'pa ānīyodagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ trir utpūya samaṃ prāṇair hṛtvottareṇāgniṃ darbheṣu sādayitvā darbhaiḥ pracchādya ||
children.translated_text: West of the fire, having brought water into a vessel covered with the pavitras, having purified it three times with the two pavitras whose tips point north, having raised it level with the vital breaths, having placed it on darbhas north of the fire, and having covered it with darbhas.
Having seated a brāhmaṇa on darbhas to the south.

children.text: ājyaṃ vilāpyāpareṇāgniṃ pavitrāntarhitāyām ājyasthālyām ājyaṃ nirupyodīco 'ṅgārān nirūhya teṣv adhiśritya jvalatāvadyutya dve darbhāgre pratyasya triḥ paryagni kṛtvodagudvāsyāṅgārān pratyūhyodagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ punar āhāraṃ trir utpūya pavitre anuprahṛtya ||
children.translated_text: Having melted the ājya, having placed the ājya in the ājya vessel west of the fire with pavitras laid within it, having drawn out embers to the north, having set it upon them, having made it shine with a blazing brand, having thrown in two tips of darbha, having carried it around the fire three times, having taken it off to the north, having put the embers back, having purified the replenished portion three times again with the two pavitras whose tips point north, and having thrown the pavitras after it.

children.text: yena juhoti tad agnau pratitapya darbhaiḥ saṃmṛjya punaḥ pratitapya prokṣya nidhāya darbhān adbhiḥ saṃspṛśyāgnau praharati ||
children.translated_text: The implement with which he offers he heats in the fire, wipes with darbhas, heats again, sprinkles, sets down, touches the darbhas with water, and throws them into the fire.
Sticks serve as enclosing pieces in marriage, initiation, return from studentship, parting of the pregnant woman's hair, first tonsure, gift of a cow, and expiations.

children.text: agniṃ pariṣiñcaty adite 'numanyasveti dakṣiṇataḥ prācīnam anumate 'numanyasveti paścād udīcīnaṃ sarasvate 'numanyasvety uttarataḥ prācīnaṃ deva savitaḥ prasuveti samantam ||
children.translated_text: He sprinkles around the fire: with 'Aditi, approve' from the south toward the east; with 'Anumati, approve' from the west toward the north; with 'Sarasvatī, approve' from the north toward the east; with 'God Savitṛ, impel' all around.
In rites for the ancestors, all around only, silently.
Having laid on the fuel, he pours the two āghāra libations as in the new- and full-moon sacrifice, silently.

children.text: athājyabhāgau juhoty agnaye svāhety uttarārdhapūrvārdhe somāya svāheti dakṣiṇārdhapūrvārdhe samaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: Then he offers the two ājya portions: 'To Agni, svāhā' in the northern half of the eastern half, and 'To Soma, svāhā' in the southern half of the eastern half, level with the first.

children.text: yathopadeśaṃ pradhānāhutīr hutvā jayābhyātānān rāṣṭrabhṛtaḥ prājāpatyāṃ vyāhṛtīr vihṛtāḥ sauviṣṭakṛtīm ity upajuhoti yad asya karmaṇo 'tyarīricaṃ yad vā nyūnam ihākaram agniṣṭakṛt sviṣṭakṛd vidvān sarvaṃ sviṣṭaṃ suhutaṃ karotu svāheti ||
children.translated_text: After offering the principal oblations according to instruction, he makes the additional offerings called the Jayas, the Abhyātānas, the Rāṣṭrabhṛts, the Prājāpatya, the separated Vyāhṛtis, and the Sauviṣṭakṛtī, saying: 'Whatever of this rite I have done in excess, or whatever deficiently here, may Agni, the maker of what is well offered, the knowing sviṣṭakṛt, make all well offered and well sacrificed. Svāhā.'

children.text: pūrvavat pariṣecanam anvamaṃsthāḥ prāsāvīr iti mantrasaṃnāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sprinkling around is as before; the adjustment of the mantras is 'you have approved' and 'you have impelled.'
The term pākayajña applies to ordinary domestic sacrifices.
There the procedure is one that has regard to a brāhmaṇa.

children.text: dvir juhoti dvir nimārṣṭi dviḥ prāśnāty utsṛtyācāmati nirleḍhīti ||
children.translated_text: He offers twice, wipes twice, eats twice; having released it, he sips water and licks clean.

children.text: sarvaṛtavo vivāhasya śaiśirau māsau parihāpyottamaṃ ca naidāgham ||
children.translated_text: All seasons are suitable for marriage, except the two wintry months and the last hot-season month.
All nakṣatras that are declared auspicious are suitable.
Likewise auspicious omens.
And they should learn from women the proper observances.
The suitors are sent forth under the Invakās, and, if welcomed, they are approved.
Cows are taken under the Maghās.
The bride is led away under the two Phalgunīs.

children.text: yāṃ kāmayeta duhitaraṃ priyāṃ syād iti tāṃ niṣṭyāyāṃ dadyāt priyaiva bhavati neva tu punar āgacchatīti brāhmaṇavekṣo vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rule having regard to a brāhmaṇa is this: the daughter whom one wishes to be beloved should be given under Niṣṭyā; she indeed becomes beloved, but does not return again.
The word Invakā denotes Mṛgaśiras.
The word Niṣṭyā denotes Svātī.
At a marriage, a cow is given.
In the houses, a cow is given.
With that cow he should honor the suitor like a guest.
The one who is less honored by her, with the other cow.

children.text: etāvad gorālambhasthānam atithiḥ pitaro vivāhaś ca ||
children.translated_text: This much is the occasion for slaughtering a cow: a guest, the ancestors, and marriage.
In choosing a bride he should avoid one who is asleep, weeping, or gone out.

children.text: dattāṃ guptāṃ dyotām ṛṣabhāṃ śarabhāṃ vinatāṃ vikaṭāṃ muṇḍāṃ maṇḍūṣikāṃ sāṅkārikāṃ rātāṃ pālīṃ mitrāṃ svanujāṃ varṣakārīṃ ca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should avoid one named Dattā, Guptā, Dyotā, Ṛṣabhā, Śarabhā, Vinatā, Vikaṭā, Muṇḍā, Maṇḍūṣikā, Sāṅkārikā, Rātā, Pālī, Mitrā, Svanujā, or Varṣakārī.
Women named after nakṣatras, rivers, or trees are censured.
And in choosing a bride he should avoid all whose names end near with r or l sounds.

children.text: śaktiviṣaye dravyāṇi praticchannāny upanidhāya brūyād upaspṛśeti ||
children.translated_text: As far as his means allow, he should place hidden objects nearby and say, 'Touch one.'

children.text: nānābījāni saṃsṛṣṭāni vedyāḥ pāṃsūn kṣetrāl loṣṭaṃ śakṛc chmaśānaloṣṭam iti ||
children.translated_text: Mixed seeds of various kinds, dust from the altar, a clod from a field, dung, and a clod from a cremation ground.
On touching the former objects, prosperity follows according to the sign.
They call the last one blameworthy.
He should marry a woman endowed with good family, character, and marks, and free from disease.
The excellence of the groom is that he is endowed with good family, character, and marks, learned, and free from disease.

children.text: yasyāṃ manaścakṣuṣor nibandhas tasyām ṛddhir netarad ādriyetety eke ||
children.translated_text: Some say: prosperity lies with the woman on whom mind and eye are fixed; one should not regard any other factor.
He should send as suitors assembled friends who know the mantras.
He should address them with the first two mantras.
Having seen her himself, he should mutter the third.
With the fourth he should look upon her.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhenopamadhyamayā cāṅgulyā darbhaṃ saṃgṛhyottareṇa yajuṣā tasyā bhruvor antaraṃ saṃmṛjya prācīnaṃ nirasyet ||
children.translated_text: Having grasped a blade of darbha grass with the thumb and the ring finger, he should wipe the space between her eyebrows with the following yajus and throw it away toward the east.
When the occasion has arrived, he should murmur the following verse.
With the following formula he should send pairs, gathered together and furnished with a mantra, to the waters.

children.text: uttareṇa yajuṣā tasyāḥ śirasi darbheṇḍvaṃ nidhāya tasminn uttarayā dakṣiṇaṃ yugacchidraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya chidre suvarṇam uttarayāntardhāyottarābhiḥ pañcabhiḥ snāpayitvottarayāhatena vāsasācchādyottarayā yoktreṇa saṃnahyati ||
children.translated_text: With the following yajus he places a darbha blade lengthwise on her head; upon it, with the following formula, he sets the right yoke-hole, conceals gold in the hole with the following formula, bathes her with the next five formulas, covers her with an unworn garment with the following formula, and binds her with the yoke-strap with the following formula.

children.text: athainām uttarayā dakṣiṇe haste gṛhītvāgnim abhyānīyāpareṇāgnim udagagraṃ kaṭam āstīrya tasminn upaviśata uttaro varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, taking her by the right hand with the following formula, he leads her toward the fire; having spread a mat west of the fire with its tips toward the north, the bridegroom sits on it, facing north.

children.text: agner upasamādhānādy ājyabhāgānte 'thainām ādito dvābhyām abhimantrayeta ||
children.translated_text: After the kindling of the fire and up to the end of the shares of ghee, he should address her first with the two following formulas.

children.text: athāsyai dakṣiṇena nīcā hastena dakṣiṇam uttānaṃ hastaṃ gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then with his right hand held low he should take her right hand, palm upward.

children.text: yadi kāmayeta strīr eva janayeyam ity aṅgulīr eva gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he should wish, 'May I beget only females,' he should take only the fingers.

children.text: yadi kāmayeta puṃsa eva janayeyam ity aṅguṣṭham eva so 'bhīvāṅguṣṭham abhīva lomāni gṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: If he should wish, 'May I beget only males,' he takes only the thumb; he grasps just the thumb, just the hairs.
He does so with these four verses beginning 'I take your hand.'

children.text: athainām uttareṇāgniṃ dakṣiṇena padā prācīm udīcīṃ vā diśam abhi prakramayaty ekam iṣa iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, north of the fire, with her right foot he makes her step toward the east or the north, with the words 'one step for nourishment.'
At the seventh step he murmurs the formula beginning 'Friend.'

children.text: prāgghomāt pradakṣiṇam agniṃ kṛtvā yathāsthānam upaviśyānvārabdhāyām uttarā āhutīr juhoti somāya janivide svāhety etaiḥ pratimantram ||
children.translated_text: Before the oblation, having gone around the fire clockwise and sat down in his proper place while she touches him, he offers the following oblations, mantra by mantra, with the formulas beginning 'To Soma, the knower of wives, svāhā.'

children.text: athainām uttareṇāgniṃ dakṣiṇena padāśmānam āsthāpayaty ātiṣṭheti ||
children.translated_text: Then, north of the fire, he makes her mount a stone with her right foot, with the formula beginning 'Mount.'

children.text: athāsyā añjalāv upastīrya dvir lājān opyābhighārayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, after spreading in her joined hands, he pours parched grain in twice and sprinkles it with ghee.
Some say that her full brother pours in the parched grain.
He offers it with the formula beginning 'This woman whom...'.

children.text: uttarābhis tisṛbhiḥ pradakṣiṇam agniṃ kṛtvāśmānam āsthāpayati yathā purastāt ||
children.translated_text: With the following three formulas he goes around the fire clockwise and makes her mount the stone, as before.
And the oblation is made with the following formula.
Again there is the circumambulation.
The mounting of the stone follows.
And the oblation is made with the following formula.
Again there is the circumambulation.
He proceeds with the formulas beginning with the jaya oblations.

children.text: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvottarābhyāṃ yoktraṃ vimucya tāṃ tataḥ pra vā vāhayet pra vā hārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite up to the final sprinkling, he unfastens the yoke-strap with the next two formulas; from there he should either have her driven forth or have her carried forth.
They take along this fire after bringing it together.
It is permanent.
It is to be maintained.
If it has gone out, it is to be produced by churning.
Or it is to be brought from the house of a learned Brahmin.
There is also fasting by either one of the two, the wife or the husband.
Or, even if the fire has gone out, he may offer with the following formula and need not fast.
The following formula is for propping up the chariot.
With the next two formulas he yokes the two draft animals, the right one first.
As she mounts, he addresses her with the following formulas.

children.text: sūtre vartmanor vyavastṛṇāty uttarayā nīlaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ lohitam uttarasyām ||
children.translated_text: He spreads two threads on the wheel-tracks with the following formula: a blue one on the southern track and a red one on the northern.
He drives over them with the following formulas.
When crossing a ford, a stump, or a crossroads, he should murmur the following formula.
With the following formula he gives assent to the boat.

children.text: na ca nāvyāṃs taratī vadhūḥ paśyet ||
children.translated_text: And the bride should not look at those who cross by boat.
After crossing, he should murmur the following formula.

children.text: śmaśānādivyatikrame bhāṇḍe rathe vā riṣṭe 'gner upasamādhānādy ājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyām uttarā āhutīr hutvā jayādi pratipadyate pariṣecanāntaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: When passing a cremation ground and the like, or when there is a mishap to a vessel, chariot, or fire, after the kindling of the fire and up to the end of the shares of ghee, while she touches him, he offers the following oblations, proceeds with the jaya formulas, and performs the rite up to the final sprinkling.

children.text: kṣīriṇām anyeṣāṃ vā lakṣmaṇyānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ nadīnāṃ dhanvanāṃ ca vyatikrama uttare yathāliṅgaṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: When passing milk-bearing trees, other auspiciously marked trees, rivers, and desert tracts, he should murmur the following formulas according to the indication.
With the following formula he makes the houses visible to her.
With the next two formulas he unyokes the two draft animals, the right one first.

children.text: lohitaṃ carmānaḍuhaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaraloma madhye 'gārasyottarayāstīrya gṛhān prapādann uttarāṃ vācayati dakṣiṇena padā ||
children.translated_text: Having spread in the middle of the house, with the following formula, a red hide of an ox, with the neck toward the east and the hair upward, he makes her enter the house with her right foot while he recites the following formula.
And she does not step upon the threshold.

children.text: uttarapūrve deśe 'gārasyāgner upasamādhānādy ājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyām uttarā āhutīr hutvā jayādi pratipadyate pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvottarayā carmaṇy upaviśata uttaro varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the northeastern part of the house, after the kindling of the fire and up to the end of the shares of ghee, while she touches him, he offers the following oblations, proceeds with the jaya formulas, performs the rite up to the final sprinkling, and with the following formula the bridegroom sits down on the hide, facing north.

children.text: athāsyāḥ puṃsvor jīvaputrāyāḥ putram aṅka uttarayopaveśya tasmai phalāny uttareṇa yajuṣā pradāyottare japitvā vācaṃ yacchata ā nakṣatrebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the following formula, he places in her lap the son of a woman who has living sons from two male children; he gives fruits to that child with the following yajus, murmurs the following formulas, and they keep silence until the stars appear.

children.text: uditeṣu nakṣatreṣu prācīm udīcīṃ vā diśam upaniṣkramyottarābhyāṃ yathāliṅgaṃ dhruvam arundhatīṃ ca darśayati ||
children.translated_text: When the stars have risen, having gone out toward the east or the north, he shows her <s>Dhruva</s> and <s>Arundhatī</s> with the next two formulas, according to the indication.
Then he has her perform worship with a cooked offering sacred to <s>Agni</s>.
The wife pounds the grain.

children.text: śrapayitvābhighārya prācīnam udīcīnaṃ vodvāsya pratiṣṭhitam abhighāryāgner upasamādhānādy ājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyāṃ sthālīpākāj juhoti ||
children.translated_text: After cooking it, sprinkling it with ghee, setting it down toward the east or the north, and sprinkling it again once it has been set down, after the kindling of the fire and up to the end of the shares of ghee, while she touches him, he offers from the cooked dish.
There is one spreading and sprinkling with ghee, and two cuttings-off of portions.
<s>Agni</s> is the deity, and the offering is made with the utterance svāhā.
Or, after touching it once, he may offer.
<s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is the second.
There is one spreading and cutting-off of a portion, and two sprinklings with ghee.
The cutting-off for the first is from the middle.
The oblation is in the middle.
For the later one, it is from the northern half.
The oblation is made in the northern half of the eastern half.

children.text: lepayoḥ prastaravat tūṣṇīṃ barhir aṅktvāgnau praharati ||
children.translated_text: Having silently anointed the barhis with the two remnants, as with the prastara, he throws it into the fire.
The subsequent sprinkling around is established.
With that, mixed with ghee, he should feed a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
To the one who has shown him honor, he gives a bull.

children.text: evam ata ūrdhvaṃ dakṣiṇāvarjam upoṣitābhyāṃ parvasu kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, from this point onward, except for the fee, the rite is to be performed on the lunar festival days by the two who have fasted.
But some say that a full vessel is the fee.

children.text: sāyaṃ prātar ata ūrdhvaṃ hastenaite āhutī taṇḍulair yavair vā juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: From this point onward, evening and morning, he should offer these two oblations by hand with rice grains or barley grains.
The deity is as in a cooked mess offering.
Some say that in the morning the first oblation is to <s>Sūrya</s>.
The sprinkling around on both sides is as before.

children.text: pārvaṇenāto 'nyāni karmāṇi vyākhyātāny ācārād yāni gṛhyante ||
children.translated_text: By the pārvaṇa rite the other rites are explained from here onward, those which are adopted according to custom.
The deities are according to the instruction.
And <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> is inserted between.
Hospitality remains unaltered.
In the vaiśvadeva rite the deities are the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>.
At the full-moon rite, the deity is the full-moon night on which it is performed.

children.text: upākaraṇe samāpane ca ṛṣir yaḥ prajñāyate ||
children.translated_text: At the opening and closing of study, the deity is the seer who is recognized.
<s>Sadasaspati</s> is the second.
They prescribe an offering for one who has not approached a woman and for one whose food is mixed with nothing worse than alkali and salt.
Optional rites and bali-offerings are according to the instruction.

children.text: sarvatra svayaṃ prajvalite 'gnāv uttarābhyāṃ samidhāv ādadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Everywhere, when the fire has kindled by itself, he should lay on the two fuel-sticks with the two following formulas.

children.text: āpan mā śrīḥ śrīr māgād iti vā ||
children.translated_text: Or with the words, 'May fortune not abandon me; may fortune come to me.'

children.text: etad ahar vijānīyād yad ahar bhāryām āvahate ||
children.translated_text: He should know that day as the day on which he brings home his wife.

children.text: trirātram ubhayor adhaḥśayyā brahmacaryaṃ kṣāralavaṇavarjanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For three nights both sleep on the ground, observe chastity, and avoid alkali and salt.

children.text: tayoḥ śayyām antareṇa daṇḍo gandhalipto vāsasā sūtreṇa vā parivītas tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Between their beds stands a staff, smeared with perfume and wrapped with a garment or a cord.

children.text: taṃ caturthyāpararātra uttarābhyām utthāpya prakṣālya nidhāyāgner upasamādhānādy ājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyām uttarā āhutīr hutvā jayādi pratipadyate pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvāpareṇāgniṃ prācīm upaveśya tasyāḥ śirasy ājyaśeṣād vyāhṛtibhir oṅkāracaturthābhir ānīyottarābhyāṃ yathāliṅgaṃ mithas samīkṣyottarayājyaśeṣeṇa hṛdayadeśau saṃmṛjyottarās tisro japitvā śeṣaṃ samāveśane japet ||
children.translated_text: In the latter part of the fourth night, having raised it with the two following formulas, washed it, and put it away, then, from the laying of the fire up to the end of the ājyabhāga offerings, while she touches him, he offers the following oblations, proceeds with the jaya and the rest, and performs the rite down to the final sprinkling around. Seating her to the west of the fire, facing east, he pours some of the remaining ghee on her head with the vyāhṛtis, with oṃ as the fourth; then with the two following formulas, according to their marks, they look at one another. With the remaining ghee from the sacrifice he wipes the regions of their hearts, recites the following three verses, and recites the remainder at the act of lying together.
Or another person may address her with the formulas.

children.text: yadā malavadvāsāḥ syād athaināṃ brāhmaṇapratiṣiddhāni karmāṇi saṃśāsti yāṃ malavadvāsasam ity etāni ||
children.translated_text: When she is wearing a stained garment, he then instructs her in the acts forbidden by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, namely the formulas beginning 'her who wears a stained garment.'

children.text: rajasaḥ prādurbhāvāt snātām ṛtusamāveśane uttarābhir abhimantrayeta ||
children.translated_text: After the appearance of menstruation, when she has bathed, at the seasonal intercourse he should address her with the following formulas.

children.text: caturthīprabhṛtyā ṣoḍaśīm uttarām uttarāṃ yugmāṃ prajāniḥśreyasam ṛtugamana ity upadiśanti ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with the fourth, up to the sixteenth, each even following night is taught as the time for seasonal approach, best for the production of offspring.

children.text: arthaprādhvasya parikṣave parikāsane cāpa upaspṛśyottare yathāliṅgaṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: On slipping, sneezing, or coughing at the chief purpose, he should touch water and recite the following verses according to their marks.

children.text: evam uttarair yathāliṅgaṃ citriyaṃ vanaspatiṃ śakṛdrīti sigvātaṃ śakunim iti ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, with the following verses according to their marks, he recites for citriya, vanaspati, śakṛdrīti, sigvāta, and śakuni.

children.text: ubhayor hṛdayasaṃsarge 'psus trirātrāvaraṃ brahmacaryaṃ caritvā sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvāgner upasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyāṃ sthālīpākād uttarā āhutīr hutvā jayādi pratipadyate pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvā tena sarpiṣmatā yugmān dvyavarān brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā siddhiṃ vācayīta ||
children.translated_text: When the hearts of the two are united, after observing chastity in water for at least three nights, he cooks a mess-offering; then, from the laying of the fire up to the end of the ājyabhāga offerings, while she touches him, he offers the following oblations from the mess, proceeds with the jaya and the rest, and performs the rite down to the final sprinkling around. With that, mixed with ghee, he feeds even-numbered <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, not fewer than two, and has success pronounced.

children.text: śvas tiṣyeṇeti triḥsaptair yavaiḥ pāṭhāṃ parikirati yadi vāruṇy asi varuṇāt tvā niṣkrīṇāmi yadi saumy asi somāt tvā niṣkrīṇāmīti ||
children.translated_text: With the words 'tomorrow, under <s>Tiṣya</s>,' he scatters pāṭhā with thrice seven barley grains, saying, 'If you belong to <s>Varuṇa</s>, I buy you off from <s>Varuṇa</s>; if you belong to <s>Soma</s>, I buy you off from <s>Soma</s>.'

children.text: śvobhūte uttarayotthāpyottarābhis tisṛbhir abhimantryottarayā praticchannāṃ hastayor ābadhya śayyākāle bāhubhyāṃ bhartāraṃ parigṛhṇīyād upadhānaliṅgayā ||
children.translated_text: On the next day he raises it with the next formula, addresses it with the next three, binds it, concealed, on her hands with the next, and at bedtime she should embrace her husband with her arms, with the formula whose mark is the pillow.
He becomes subject to her will.
And there is the removal of a co-wife.
With this same desire, using the following anuvāka, he continually worships <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: yakṣmagṛhītām anyāṃ vā brahmacaryayuktaḥ puṣkarasaṃvartamūlair uttarair yathāliṅgam aṅgāni saṃmṛśya pratīcīnaṃ nirasyet ||
children.translated_text: Practicing chastity, he should touch, according to the marks of the following formulas, the limbs of a woman seized by wasting disease or another illness with roots of puṣkarasaṃvarta, and cast the ailment away westward.
With the following formulas he should give the bride's garment to one who knows this rite.
We shall explain initiation.
He should initiate a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the eighth year from conception.
A <s>Rājanya</s> in the eleventh year from conception, and a <s>Vaiśya</s> in the twelfth year from conception.

children.text: vasanto grīṣmaḥ śarad ity ṛtavo varṇānupūrvyeṇa ||
children.translated_text: Spring, summer, and autumn are the seasons, in the order of the social classes.

children.text: brāhmaṇān bhojayitvāśiṣo vācayitvā kumāraṃ bhojayitvānuvākasya prathamena yajuṣāpaḥ saṃsṛjyoṣṇāḥ śītāsv ānīyottarayā śira unatti ||
children.translated_text: Having fed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, had blessings pronounced, and fed the boy, he mixes water with the first yajus of the anuvāka, pours hot water into cold, and with the next formula moistens the boy's head.

children.text: trīṃs trīn darbhān antardhāyottarābhiś catasṛbhiḥ pratimantraṃ pratidiśaṃ pravapati ||
children.translated_text: Placing three darbha blades at a time between, with the next four formulas, one for each mantra and one for each direction, he cuts the hair.

children.text: vapantam uttarayānumantrayate dakṣiṇato mātā brahmacārī vā ||
children.translated_text: With the next formula the mother, or a brahmacārin, standing to the south, addresses the one who is cutting.

children.text: ānaḍuhe śakṛtpiṇḍe yavān nidhāya tasmin keśān upayamyottarayodumbaramūle darbhastambe vā nidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Having placed barley grains on a lump of bull's dung, he gathers the hair onto it and, with the next formula, deposits it at the root of an udumbara tree or in a clump of darbha.

children.text: snātam agner upasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte pālāśīṃ samidham uttarayādhāpyottareṇāgniṃ dakṣiṇena padāśmānam āsthāpayaty ātiṣṭheti ||
children.translated_text: After the boy has bathed, from the laying of the fire up to the end of the ājyabhāga offerings, he has him place a palāśa fuel-stick with the next formula; then, north of the fire, he makes him step with his right foot on a stone, saying, 'Step upon it.'

children.text: vāsaḥsadyaḥkṛttotam uttarābhyām abhimantryottarābhis tisṛbhiḥ paridhāpya parihitam uttarayānumantrayate ||
children.translated_text: Having consecrated the garment, freshly cut, with the next two formulas, and having clothed him with the next three formulas, he addresses him, once clothed, with the next formula.

children.text: mauñjīṃ mekhalāṃ trivṛtāṃ triḥpradakṣiṇam uttarābhyāṃ parivīyājinam uttaram uttarayā ||
children.translated_text: He winds a triple girdle of muñja grass around him three times clockwise with the next two formulas; the antelope skin is the next item, with the next formula.

children.text: uttareṇāgniṃ darbhān saṃstīrya teṣv enam uttarayāvasthāpyodakāñjalim asmā añjalāv ānīyottarayā triḥ prokṣyottarair dakṣiṇe haste gṛhītvottarair devatābhyaḥ paridāyottareṇa yajuṣopanīya suprajā iti dakṣiṇe karṇe japati ||
children.translated_text: Having spread darbha grass north of the fire, he sets him upon it with the next formula; bringing a handful of water into his cupped hands, he sprinkles him three times with the next formula; grasping him by the right hand with the following formulas, handing him over to the deities with the following formulas, and initiating him with the following yajus, he whispers 'May you have good offspring' into his right ear.
The boy says, 'I have come to <s>brahmacarya</s> (studenthood).'
When asked, the boy gives his answer to the other person.
The rest the other person recites softly.
And he makes him pronounce a blessing turned toward himself.
The procedure up to the end of the ājyabhāga offerings has been stated.

children.text: atrainam uttarā āhutīr hāvayitvā jayādi pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, after having him offer the following oblations, he proceeds with the jaya and the rest.

children.text: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvāpareṇāgnim udagagraṃ kūrcaṃ nidhāya tasminn uttareṇa yajuṣopanetopaviśati ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite down to the final sprinkling around, he places a bundle of darbha grass with its tips to the north, west of the fire; on it, the initiated boy sits down with the following yajus.

children.text: purastāt pratyaṅṅ āsīnaḥ kumāro dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇaṃ pādam anvārabhyāha sāvitrīṃ bho anubrūhi iti ||
children.translated_text: The boy, seated in front and facing west, touches the right foot with his right hand and says, 'Sir, recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> to me.'
He recites it to him, beginning 'tat savitur.'
First by pādas, then by half-verses, and then the whole of it.

children.text: vyāhṛtīr vihṛtāḥ pādādiṣv anteṣu vā tathārdharcayor uttamāṃ kṛtsnāyām ||
children.translated_text: The vyāhṛtis are inserted separately at the beginnings of the pādas or at their ends; likewise, at the two half-verses, and the last one at the complete verse.
The boy touches his upper lip with the next mantra.
His ears with the next.
He takes the staff with the next.

children.text: pālāśo daṇḍo brāhmaṇasya naiyagrodhaḥ skandhajo 'vāgagro rājanyasya bādara audumbaro vā vaiśyasya ||
children.translated_text: The staff of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is of palāśa; that of a <s>Rājanya</s> is a branch-born staff of nyagrodha, with its tip downward; that of a <s>Vaiśya</s> is of badara or udumbara.
Some teach, without connection to social class, that the staff should simply be of tree-wood.

children.text: smṛtaṃ ca ma ity etad vācayitvā gurave varaṃ dattvod āyuṣety utthāpyottarair ādityam upatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: Having made him recite the words beginning 'smṛtaṃ ca me,' and after he has given a gift to the teacher, he raises him with 'ud āyuṣā' and, with the following formulas, worships <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta nāyam āchidyeteti tam uttarayā dakṣiṇe haste gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: The one whom he wishes not to be torn away, he should grasp by the right hand with the next formula.
They maintain this fire for three days.
And there is avoidance of alkali and salt.

children.text: pari tveti parimṛjya tasminn uttarair mantraiḥ samidha ādadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having wiped around with 'pari tvā,' he should place fuel-sticks on that fire with the following mantras.

children.text: evam anyasminn api sadāraṇyād edhān āhṛtya ||
children.translated_text: In the same way also on another fire, after bringing fuel from the forest.
He instructs him with the next formula.
On the fourth day he takes off the garment with the next formula, after having clothed him in another.
Now the section on the opening and closing of Vedic study. Now, then, we shall explain the opening and closing of study.

children.text: śravaṇāpakṣa oṣadhīṣu jātāsu hastena paurṇamāsyāṃ vādhyāyopākarma ||
children.translated_text: In the fortnight of <s>Śravaṇa</s>, when the herbs have appeared, or on the full-moon day under <s>Hasta</s>, the opening of study takes place.

children.text: agner upasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdheṣu kāṇḍaṛṣibhyo juhoti sadasaspataye sāvitryā ṛgvedāya yajurvedāya sāmavedāyātharvaṇavedāyeti hutvā upahomo vedāhutīn āmupariṣṭāt sadasaspatim ity eke ||
children.translated_text: From the laying of the fire up to the end of the ājyabhāga offerings, while they are touching him, he offers to the seers of the kāṇḍas: to <s>Sadasaspati</s>, to the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, to the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, to the <s>Yajurveda</s>, to the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and to the <s>Atharvaveda</s>. Having offered thus, there is an additional oblation. Some say that the Vedic oblations are after this, and <s>Sadasaspati</s> afterward.
Having performed the rite down to the final sprinkling around, they should study the first three anuvākas from the beginning.
Or the first and last anuvākas.
For three days, or for one day, they should study as much as is possible.
Now the chapter on the opening of study.
The closing of study takes place in the fortnight of <s>Taiṣa</s>, under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, or on the full-moon day.

children.text: prācīm udīcīṃ vā sagaṇo diśam upaniṣkramya yatrāpaḥ purastātsukhāḥ sukhāvagāhā avakinyaḥ śaṅkhinyaḥ tāsāmantaṃ gatvā 'bhiṣekānkṛtvā surabhimatyābliṅgābhirvāruṇībhirhiraṇyavarṇābhiḥ pāvamanībhiriti mārjayitvāntarjalagato 'ghamarṣaṇena trīnprāṇāyāmān dhārayitvottīryācamyopotthāya darbhānanyonyasmai sampradāya śucau deśe prākkūlairdarbhairāsanāni kalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Together with his group, he goes out toward the east or north, to a place where water lies pleasantly in front, is easy to enter, has no mud, and has shells. Having gone to its edge, performed ablutions, and cleansed himself with the fragrant verses, or with the waters verses, the Varuṇa verses, the golden-colored verses, and the purifying verses, he enters the water, holds three breath-controls with the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>, comes out, sips water, rises, and, after they have handed darbha grasses to one another, they prepare seats in a clean place with darbha grasses whose tips face east.

children.text: brahmaṇe prajāpataye vṛhaspataye 'gnaye vāyave sūryāya candramase nakṣatrebhyaḥ ṛtubhyassaṃvatsarāya indrāya rājñe somāya rājñe yamāya rājñe varuṇāya rājñe vaiśravaṇāya rājñe vasubhyo rudrebhya ādityebhyo viśvebhyo devebhyassādhyebhyo marudbhya ṛbhubhyo bhṛgubhyo 'ṅgirobhya iti devagaṇānām ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Vṛhaspati</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Candramas</s>, the constellations, the seasons, the year, king <s>Indra</s>, king <s>Soma</s>, king <s>Yama</s>, king <s>Varuṇa</s>, king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, all the gods, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Ṛbhus</s>, <s>Bhṛgus</s>, and <s>Aṅgirases</s>: this is for the hosts of deities.

children.text: atharṣayaḥviśvāmitro jamadagnirbharadvājo gautamo 'trirvasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapa ityete saptarṣayaḥ saptarṣibhyaḥ kalpayitvā dakṣiṇato 'gastyāya kalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Next, the seers: <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s>; these are the seven seers. Having prepared a place for the seven seers, they prepare one to the south for <s>Agastya</s>.
Then they prepare places for as many as are teachers of a single Veda.

children.text: prācīnāvītāni kṛtvā dakṣiṇato vaiśampāyanāya paiṅgaye tittiraye ukhāyātreyāya padākārāya kauṇḍinyāya vṛttikārāya baudhāyanāya pravacanakārāya āpastambāya sūtrakārāya bharadvājāya sūtrakārāya satyāṣāḍhāya hiraṇyakeśāya ācāryebhya ūrdhvaretobhya ekapatnībhyo vānaprasthebhyaḥ kalpayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Having put the sacred thread over the right shoulder, they prepare to the south for <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, <s>Paiṅga</s>, <s>Tittiri</s>, <s>Ukha</s>, <s>Ātreya</s>, the maker of the pada text, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the commentator, <s>Baudhāyana</s>, the expounder, <s>Āpastamba</s>, the sūtra-maker, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, the sūtra-maker, <s>Satyāṣāḍha</s>, <s>Hiraṇyakeśin</s>, the teachers, those of upward-flowing seed, those with one wife, and the forest-dwellers, saying, 'I prepare places.'

children.text: atha yathāsvaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ kalpayanti mātāmahebhyaśca pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: Then they prepare places separately for their own fathers and for their maternal grandfathers.

children.text: yajñopavītāni kṛtvā teṣveva deśeṣu tathaivānupūrvyā taireva nāmabhirdevānṛṣīṃśca tarpayanti vaiśampāyanaprabhṛtīṃstu mātuḥ prapitāmahaparyantānprācīnāvītinastarpayanti amuṃ tarpayāmyamuṃ tarpayāmyamuṃ tarpayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Having put on the sacred thread, in those same places and in the same order, with those same names, they satisfy the gods and seers with water; but, wearing the thread over the right shoulder, they satisfy the ancestors beginning with <s>Vaiśampāyana</s> down to the mother's great-grandfather, saying, "I satisfy this one, I satisfy this one, I satisfy this one."
Or they may sprinkle one another.
Having put on the sacred threads, they should recite the first three anuvākas from the beginning.
Or the first and last portions beginning the kāṇḍas.
With the two verses beginning "From joint to joint you sprout," they plant dūrvā grass near water.
Entering the waters, they make a sea.
Enclosing it on all sides, they make waves.
Having come out, they run along an unmeasured line.
On returning, after feeding <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with the invitations, with roasted meal, and with cooked rice, he has them recite.
So too at the completion of a pārāyaṇa, except for the kāṇḍa-beginning recitation, the planting of dūrvā, and the running in the sea.
On returning, he undertakes the rite beginning with the feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

children.text: evam evādbhir ahar ahar devān ṛṣīnpitīṃśca tarpayet ||
children.translated_text: In just this way, with water, day after day, he should satisfy the gods, seers, and ancestors.

children.text: vedam adhītya snāsyan prāgudayād vrajaṃ praviśyāntarlomnā carmaṇā dvāram apidhāyāste ||
children.translated_text: When he has studied the Veda and is about to bathe, before sunrise he enters a cow-pen, closes the door with a hide whose hair faces inward, and sits there.
On that day the sun should not shine upon him.

children.text: madhyandine 'gner upasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte pālāśīṃ samidham uttarayādhāyāpareṇāgniṃ kaṭa erakāyāṃ vopaviśyottarayā kṣuram abhimantryottareṇa yajuṣā vaptre pradāyāpāṃ saṃsarjanādy ā keśanidhānāt samānam ||
children.translated_text: At midday, after the laying of the fire up to the end of the ājyabhāga offerings, he places a palāśa fuel-stick with the following formula; sitting west of the fire on a mat or on erakā grass, he consecrates the razor with the following formula, gives it to the barber with the following yajus, and the procedure from the mixing of the waters up to the depositing of the hair is the same.

children.text: jaghanārdhe vrajasyopaviśya visrasya mekhalāṃ brahmacāriṇe prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: Sitting in the rear half of the cow-pen, he loosens the girdle and gives it to a brahmacārin.

children.text: tāṃ sa uttareṇa yajuṣodumbaramūle darbhastambe vopagūhati ||
children.translated_text: With the following yajus, that student conceals it at the root of an udumbara tree or in a clump of darbha.

children.text: evaṃ vihitābhir evādbhir uttarābhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ snātvottarayodumbareṇa dato dhāvate ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed with these very prescribed waters and with the following six formulas, he cleans his teeth with an udumbara twig with the following formula.
He is covered with bathing paste and bathed.

children.text: uttarena yajuṣā 'hatam antaraṃ vāsaḥ paridhāya sārvasurabhiṇā candanenottarair devatābhyaḥ pradāyottarayānulipya maṇiṃ sauvarṇaṃ sopadhānaṃ sūtrotam uttarayodapātre triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ pariplāvyottarayā grīvāsv ābadhyaivam eva bādaraṃ maṇiṃ mantravarjaṃ savye pāṇāv ābadhyāhatam uttaraṃ vāso revatīs tveti samānam ||
children.translated_text: With the following yajus he puts on a new lower garment; with sandalwood of every fragrance, after offering to the deities with the following formulas, he anoints himself with the following formula; with the following formula he plunges a gold jewel, furnished with a setting and strung on a thread, three times clockwise in a water vessel, ties it on his necks with the following formula, and in the same way, but without a mantra, ties a badara jewel on his left hand. The new upper garment is as before, with the formula beginning "Revatīs are you."

children.text: tasya daśāyāṃ pravartau prabadhya darvyām ādhāyājyenābhyānāyann uttarā āhutīr hutvā jayādi pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: Having tied two tassels on its fringe, placed it on a ladle, and anointed it with ghee, he offers the following oblations and proceeds with the jaya and the rest.

children.text: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvā tābhir eva dakṣiṇe karṇa ābadhnītaitābhiḥ savye ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite down to the final sprinkling around, he should tie them on the right ear with those same formulas and on the left with these.

children.text: evam uttarair yathāliṅgaṃ srajaḥ śirasy āñjanam ādarśāvekṣaṇam upānahau chatraṃ daṇḍam iti ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, with the following formulas according to their marks, he deals with garlands on the head, collyrium, looking in a mirror, sandals, an umbrella, and a staff.
He restrains his speech until the stars appear.

children.text: uditeṣu nakṣatreṣu prācīm udīcīṃ vā diśam upaniṣkramyottareṇārdharcena diśa upasthāyottareṇa nakṣatrāṇi candramasam iti ||
children.translated_text: When the stars have risen, going out toward the east or north, he worships the directions with the following half-verse, and the stars and the moon with the following formula.
Having conversed with the night, he goes where he has business.

children.text: athaitad aparaṃ tūṣṇīm eva tīrthe snātvā tūṣṇīṃ samidham ādadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Now this is another procedure: silently, having bathed at a ford, he silently places a fuel-stick.

children.text: yatrāsmā apacitiṃ kurvanti tat kūrca upaviśati yathāpurastāt ||
children.translated_text: Where they show him honor, he sits on a bunch of grass, as before.

children.text: evam uttarābhyāṃ yathāliṅgaṃ rājā sthapatiś ca ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, with the following two formulas according to their marks, a king and a chieftain are treated.
He says, "Water for the feet."

children.text: uttarayābhimantrya dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇāya prayacchet savyaṃ śūdrāya ||
children.translated_text: Having consecrated it with the following formula, he should present the right foot first to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, but the left to a <s>Śūdra</s>.
Having touched the person who washes his feet, with the following yajus he should touch himself in return.

children.text: kūrcābhyāṃ parigṛhya mṛnmayenārhaṇīyā āpa iti prāha ||
children.translated_text: Taking it with two bunches of grass and with an earthen vessel, he says, "The water worthy of honor."

children.text: uttarayābhimantryāñjalāv ekadeśa ānīyamāna uttaraṃ yajur japet ||
children.translated_text: Having consecrated it with the following formula, when a portion is brought into his joined hands, he mutters the following yajus.
When the remainder is poured out in front, he approves it with the following formula.

children.text: dadhi madhv iti saṃsṛjya kāṃsyena varṣīyasā pidhāya kūrcābhyāṃ parigṛhya madhuparka iti prāha ||
children.translated_text: Having mixed curds and honey, covered it with a larger bronze vessel, and taken it with two bunches of grass, he says, "Madhuparka."
Some make it threefold, and add ghee.
Some make it fivefold, adding grains and roasted meal.

children.text: uttarābhyām abhimantrya yajurbhyām apa ācāmati purastād upariṣṭāc cottarayā triḥ prāśyānukampyāya prayacchet ||
children.translated_text: Having consecrated it with the following two yajus formulas, he sips water before and after; with the following formula, after tasting it three times, he should give it to one toward whom compassion is due.
A king or chieftain, after receiving it, gives it to the purohita.
Saying "A cow," he announces the cow.

children.text: uttarayābhimantrya tasyai vapāṃ śrapayitvopastīrṇābhighāritāṃ madhyamenāntamena vā palāśaparṇenottarayā juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Having consecrated it with the following formula, he cooks its omentum; after it has been laid on and sprinkled with ghee, he offers it with the following formula by means of the middle or last palāśa leaf.

children.text: yady utsṛjed upāṃśūttarāṃ japitvom utsṛjatety uccaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he releases it, after silently muttering the following formula, he says aloud, "Release it."

children.text: annaṃ proktam upāṃśūttarair abhimantryoṃ kalpayatety uccaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When food has been announced, having silently consecrated it with the following formulas, he says aloud, "Prepare it."

children.text: ācāryāyartvije śvaśurāya rājña iti parisaṃvatsarād upatiṣṭhadbhya etat kāryam ||
children.translated_text: This is to be done for a teacher, an officiating priest, a father-in-law, or a king when they come after the passing of a full year.
For a teacher of recitation and for <s>Citra</s>, it is done once.
The sīmantonnayana, in the section on pregnancy, is in the fourth month of pregnancy.

children.text: brāhmaṇān bhojayitvāśiṣo vācayitvāgner upasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte 'nvārabdhāyāmuttarā āhutīrhutvā jayādi pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: Having fed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, had blessings pronounced, and, after the laying of the fire up to the end of the ājyabhāga offerings, while she touches him, he offers the following oblations and proceeds with the jaya and the rest.

children.text: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvāpareṇāgniṃ prācīnamupaveśya treṇyā śalalyā tribhir darbhapuñjīlaiḥ śalāluglapsenetyūrdhvaṃ sīmantamunnayati vyāhṛtībhir uttarābhyāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite down to the final sprinkling around, he seats her eastward to the west of the fire and, with a threefold porcupine quill, with three bunches of darbha, and with a bunch of unripe udumbara fruits, saying, "śalāluglapsa," he parts the hair upward with the vyāhṛtis and with the following two formulas.
He instructs the two lute-singers, "Sing."
Of the following two songs, the first belongs to the <s>Sālva</s> <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the other to the others.
There is also the mention of the river on which they live.

children.text: yavān virūḍhān ābadhya vācaṃ yacchaty ā nakṣatrebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having tied on sprouted barley grains, he restrains speech until the stars appear.

children.text: uditeṣu nakṣatreṣu prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya vatsamanvārabhya vyāhṛtīśca japitvā vācaṃ visṛjet ||
children.translated_text: When the stars have risen, going out toward the east or north and touching a calf, after muttering the vyāhṛtis he should release speech.
The <s>puṃsavana</s> is performed when the embryo is perceptible, under the <s>Tiṣya</s> asterism.

children.text: nyagrodhasya yā prācyudīcī vā śākhā tataḥ savṛṣaṇāṃ śuṅgāmāhṛtya sīmantavadagnerupasamādhānādi ||
children.translated_text: From a branch of a banyan tree that points eastward or northward, he brings a shoot together with its pair of fruits, and the procedure, beginning with the placing of the fire, is as in the sīmantonnayana.

children.text: anavasnātayā kumāryā dṛṣatputre dṛṣatputreṇa peṣayitvā pariplāvyāpareṇāgniṃ prācīmuttānāṃ nipātyottareṇa yajuṣāṅguṣṭhena dakṣiṇe nāsikāchidre 'pinayati ||
children.translated_text: Having had it ground on a grinding stone by an unmarried girl who has not bathed, and having mixed it, he lays the woman on her back, eastward, to the west of the fire, and with the following yajus he introduces it with his thumb into her right nostril.
It causes a male child to be born.
It brings about quick delivery.

children.text: anāprītena śarāveṇānusrotasam udakam āhṛtya pattastūryantīṃ nidhāya mūrdhañchoṣyantīm uttareṇa yajuṣābhimṛśyaitābhir adbhir uttarābhir avokṣet ||
children.translated_text: Bringing water with the current in an unbaked bowl, placing the woman who is in labor on a bed, and touching her head as she is about to become dry with the following yajus, he should sprinkle her with these waters using the following formulas.

children.text: yadi jarāyu na pated evaṃvihitābhir evādbhir uttarābhyām avokṣet ||
children.translated_text: If the afterbirth does not fall, he should sprinkle it with these same prescribed waters using the following two formulas.

children.text: jātaṃ vātsapreṇābhimṛśyottareṇa yajuṣopastha ādhāyottarābhyām abhimantraṇaṃ mūrdhanyavaghrāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe karṇe jāpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having touched the newborn with the <s>Vātsapra</s> formula, he places it in the lap with the following yajus; with the following two formulas there is address to it, smelling its head, and muttering in its right ear.
He also states the name of the asterism.
That becomes secret.

children.text: madhu ghṛtamiti saṃsṛjya tasmin darbheṇa hiraṇyaṃ niṣṭarkyaṃ baddhvāvadāyottarair mantraiḥ kumāraṃ prāśayitvottarābhiḥ pañcabhiḥ snāpayitvā dadhi ghṛtamiti saṃsṛjya kāṃsyena pṛṣadājyaṃ vyāhṛtībhir oṅkāracaturthābhiḥ kumāraṃ prāśayitvādbhiḥ śeṣaṃ saṃsṛjya goṣṭhe ninayet ||
children.translated_text: Having mixed honey and ghee, tied a flawless piece of gold to darbha in it and dipped it out, he makes the boy taste it with the following mantras; after bathing him with the following five formulas, mixing curds and ghee, and preparing pṛṣadājya in a bronze vessel, he makes the boy taste it with the vyāhṛtis, with <s>oṃ</s> as the fourth, mixes the remainder with water, and pours it in the cow-pen.

children.text: uttarayā māturupastha ādhāyottarayā dakṣiṇaṃ stanaṃ pratidhāpyottarābhyāṃ pṛthivīmabhimṛśyottareṇa yajuṣā saṃviṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: With the following formula he places him in the mother's lap; with the following one he gives him the right breast; with the following two he touches the earth; and with the following yajus he lays him down.

children.text: uttareṇa yajuṣā śirasta udakumbhaṃ nidhāya sarṣapān phalīkaraṇamiśrān añjalinottarais tristriḥ pratisvāhākāraṃ hutvā saṃśāsti praviṣṭe praviṣṭa eva tūṣṇīmagnāvāvapateti ||
children.translated_text: With the following yajus he places a water jar near his head, then, with a handful of mustard seeds mixed with parched grain, he offers them with the following formulas three times each, with a svāhā-call each time, and instructs: "Whenever anyone has entered, then, after he has entered, silently cast them into the fire."
In this way day after day until the tenth day.

children.text: daśamyāmutthitāyāṃ snātāyāṃ putrasya nāma dadhāti pitā māteti ||
children.translated_text: On the tenth day, when the mother has risen and bathed, the father and mother give the son his name.

children.text: dvyakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃ vā nāmapūrvamākhyātottaraṃ dīrghābhiniṣṭhānāntaṃ ghoṣavadādyantarantastham ||
children.translated_text: The name should have two syllables or four syllables; it should have a noun first and a verbal form after, end in a long vowel or visarga, and have a voiced sound at the beginning, with a semivowel in the middle or at the end.

children.text: api vā yasmin svityupasargaḥ syāt taddhi pratiṣṭhitamiti hi brāhmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Or else it may be a name in which the prefix su occurs, for that is well established; so says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
For a girl it should have an odd number of syllables.

children.text: pravāsādetya putrasyottarābhyāmabhimantraṇaṃ mūrdhanyavaghrāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe karṇa uttarānmantrān japet ||
children.translated_text: Having returned from a journey, he should address his son with the following two formulas, smell his head, and mutter the following mantras in his right ear.
He addresses a daughter with the following yajus.

children.text: janmano 'dhi ṣaṣṭhe māsi brāhmaṇān bhojayitvāśiṣo vācayitvā dadhi madhu ghṛtam odanam iti saṃsṛjyottarair mantraiḥ kumāraṃ prāśayet ||
children.translated_text: In the sixth month from birth, after feeding <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and having blessings pronounced, he should mix curds, honey, ghee, and cooked rice, and with the following mantras make the boy taste it.
Some say: with the meat of a francolin.
In the third year from birth, the caula tonsure is performed under the two <s>Punarvasu</s> stars.
The feeding of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> is as at the initiation.
The procedure beginning with the placing of the fire is as in the sīmantonnayana.

children.text: apareṇāgniṃ prāñcam upaveśya treṇyā śalalyā tribhir darbhapuñjīlaiḥ śalāluglapseneti tūṣṇīṃ keśān vinīya yatharṣi śikhā nidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Having seated him facing east to the west of the fire, he silently parts the hair with a threefold porcupine quill, with three bunches of darbha, and with a bunch of unripe udumbara fruits, saying, "śalāluglapsa," and arranges the topknot according to the seer.
It should be according to the family custom of these people.
The procedure from the mixing of the waters up to the depositing of the hair is the same.
He washes the razor and puts it down.
With that, there is abstention from ritual activity for three days.
He gives a gift.

children.text: evaṃ godānam anyasminn api nakṣatre ṣoḍaśe varṣe ||
children.translated_text: In this same way the godāna rite is performed, also under another asterism, in the sixteenth year.
Or it may be the agnigodāna.
Some prescribe the godāna-vow for a year.
Only this much is different: he has all the hair shaved.
The <s>Chandogas</s> say that there is touching of water.

children.text: dakṣiṇāpratyakpravaṇam agārāvakāśam uddhatya palāśena śamīmayena vodūhenaitām eva diśam uttarayodūhati ||
children.translated_text: Having cleared a space for the house, sloping to the south and west, he sweeps this same direction with a broom made of palāśa or śamī wood, using the following formula.
In this way three times.

children.text: kﾱptam uttarayābhimṛśya pradakṣiṇaṃ sthūṇāgartān khānayitvābhyantaraṃ pāṃsūn udupyottarābhyāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dvārasthūṇām avadadhāti ||
children.translated_text: After touching the prepared place with the following formula, he has the post-holes dug clockwise, throws the earth inward, and with the following two formulas sets down the southern door-post.
In this same way he sets down the other one.

children.text: yathākhātam itarā anvavadhāya vaṃśam ādhīyamānam uttareṇa yajuṣābhimantrayate ||
children.translated_text: Having set down the other posts according to the holes dug, he addresses the ridge-pole as it is being placed with the following yajus.
When it has been measured together, he addresses it with the following formulas according to their marks.

children.text: pālāśaṃ śamīmayaṃ vedhmam ādīpyottarayarcāgnim uddhṛtyottareṇa yajuṣāgāraṃ prapādyottarapūrvadeśe 'gārasyottarayāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: Having kindled fuel of palāśa or śamī wood, drawn out the fire with the following verse, and brought it into the house with the following yajus, he establishes the fire in the northeastern part of the house with the following formula.
To the south of that is the place for the water vessel.

children.text: tasmin viṣūcīnāgrān darbhān saṃstīrya teṣūttarayā vrīhiyavān nyupya tatrodadhānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: Having spread darbha grasses there with their tips pointing in different directions, he pours rice and barley on them with the following formula, and sets the vessel for water there.

children.text: tasminn uttareṇa yajuṣā catura udakumbhān ānayati ||
children.translated_text: Into it he brings four water jars with the next yajus formula.
With the next formula he addresses what is split or cracked.

children.text: agner upasamādhānādyājyabhāgānte uttarā āhutīr hutvā jayādi pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with the laying of the fire, after the ājyabhāga offerings, having offered the following oblations, he proceeds with the jaya and the rest.

children.text: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvottareṇa yajuṣodakumbhena triḥ pradakṣiṇam antarato 'gāraṃ niveśanaṃ vā pariṣicya brāhmaṇān bhojayed apūpaiḥ saktubhir odaneneti ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite down to the final sprinkling around, with the water jar and the following yajus he sprinkles three times clockwise, from inside, the house or dwelling, and should feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with cakes, roasted meal, and cooked rice.

children.text: śvagrahagṛhītaṃ kumāraṃ tapoyukto jālena pracchādya kaṃsaṃ kiṅkiṇiṃ vā hrādayann advāreṇa sabhāṃ prapādya sabhāyā madhye 'dhidevanam uddhatyāvokṣyākṣān nyupyākṣeṣūttānaṃ nipātya dadhnā lavaṇamiśreṇāñjalinottarair avokṣet prātar madhyandine sāyam ||
children.translated_text: A child seized by a dog-demon: being under observance, he covers the child with a net, and, making a bronze vessel or a little bell resound, brings him into the assembly-hall through a place that is not the door; in the middle of the assembly-hall he clears and sprinkles the gaming-place, scatters dice, lays the child face upward on the dice, and should sprinkle him from joined hands with curds mixed with salt, using the following formulas, in the morning, at midday, and in the evening.
He becomes free from illness.

children.text: śaṅkhinaṃ kumāraṃ tapoyukta uttarābhyām abhimantryottarayodakumbhena śirasto 'vanayet prātar madhyandine sāyam ||
children.translated_text: For a child with shell-like swelling, being under observance, he addresses him with the following two formulas, and with the following formula pours water from a water jar down from his head in the morning, at midday, and in the evening.
He becomes free from illness.
On the full-moon day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, after sunset, there is a sthālīpāka offering.

children.text: pārvaṇavad ājyabhāgānte sthālīpākāddhutvāñjalinottaraiḥ pratimantraṃ kiṃśukāni juhoti ||
children.translated_text: As at a parvan rite, after the ājyabhāga offerings, having offered from the sthālīpāka, he offers kiṃśuka blossoms with each of the following mantras from his joined hands.
With the following three formulas he offers fuel-sticks of āragvadha wood.
The following are oblations of ghee.
He proceeds with the jaya and the rest.

children.text: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvā vāgyataḥ saṃbhārān ādāya prācīm udīcīṃ vā diśam upaniṣkramyasthaṇḍilaṃ kalpayitvā tatra prācīr udīcīś ca tisras tisro lekhā likhitvādbhir upaninīya tāsūttarayā saktūn nivapati ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite down to the final sprinkling around, silently taking the materials, going out toward the east or north, and preparing a sthaṇḍila, he draws there three lines each toward the east and north, brings water to them, and with the following formula pours roasted meal upon them.

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ saṃpuṣkā dhānā lājān āñjanābhyañjane sthagarośīram iti ||
children.translated_text: Silently he adds saṃpuṣka, grains, parched grain, collyrium, unguent, sthagara, and uśīra.

children.text: uttarair upasthāyāpaḥ pariṣicyāpratīkṣas tūṣṇīm etyāpaśveta padety ābhyām udakumbhena triḥ pradakṣiṇam antarato 'gāraṃ niveśanaṃ vā pariṣicya brāhmaṇān bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped with the following formulas and sprinkled water around, without looking back he silently returns; and with the two formulas beginning 'May the waters be white-footed,' he sprinkles three times clockwise, from inside, the house or dwelling with a water jar, and should feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
They make the children eat the grains.

children.text: evam ata ūrdhvaṃ yadaśanīyasya saktūnāṃ vaitaṃ baliṃ hared ā mārgaśīrṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way from then onward, whenever there is something edible, or roasted meal, he should offer this bali until the <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> full moon.
On the full-moon day of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, after sunset, there is a sthālīpāka offering.
The adaptation of the bali-mantra is 'I have brought it.'
At this point he releases it.
The first-fruits offering of one who has not established the sacred fires follows.

children.text: navānāṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvāgrayaṇadevatābhyaḥ sviṣṭakṛccaturthābhyo hutvā taṇḍulānāṃ mukhaṃ pūrayitvā gīrtvācamyaudanapiṇḍaṃ saṃvṛtyottareṇa yajuṣāgārastūpa udviddhet ||
children.translated_text: Having cooked a sthālīpāka of new grain, having offered to the deities of the first-fruits rite, with Sviṣṭakṛt as the fourth, he fills his mouth with rice-grains, swallows them, sips water, wraps up a lump of cooked rice, and with the following yajus throws it up onto the roof of the house.
The winter descent follows.

children.text: uttareṇa yajuṣā pratyavaruhyottarair dakṣiṇaiḥ pārśvaiḥ navasvastare saṃviśanti ||
children.translated_text: Having descended with the following yajus, they lie down on a new layer with the following formulas, on their right sides.

children.text: dakṣiṇataḥ pitottarā mātaivam avaśiṣṭānāṃ jyeṣṭho jyeṣṭho 'nantaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The father lies to the south, the mother to the north; in the same way, among the remaining persons, the eldest lies next in order.
Having come together, they touch the earth with the following two formulas.
Thus the procedure beginning with lying down is done three times.

children.text: īśānāya sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā kṣaitrapatyaṃ ca prācīm udīcīṃ vā diśam upaniṣkramya sthaṇḍilaṃ kalpayitvāgner upasamādhānādi ||
children.translated_text: Having cooked a sthālīpāka for <s>Īśāna</s> and also one for the lord of the field, going out toward the east or north, preparing a sthaṇḍila, and beginning with the laying of the fire...
To the west of the fire he makes two huts.
With the following formula he invokes <s>Īśāna</s> in the southern one.
With ordinary speech he invokes <s>Mīḍhuṣī</s> in the northern one.
In the middle he invokes <s>Jayanta</s>.

children.text: yathoḍham udakāni pradāya trīn odanān kalpayitvāgnim abhy ānīyottarair upasparśayitvā uttarair yathāsvam odanebhyo hutvā sarvataḥ samavadāyottareṇa yajuṣāgniṃ sviṣṭakṛtam
children.translated_text: Having given water according to the way they have been placed, prepared three portions of cooked rice, brought the fire near, touched them with the following formulas, and offered from each rice portion with the following formulas as appropriate, he takes portions from all sides and with the following yajus offers to <s>Agni</s> Sviṣṭakṛt.

children.text: uttareṇa yajuṣopasthāyottaraiḥ sahodanāni parṇāny ekaikena dve dve dattvā devasenābhyo daśottarābhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped with the following yajus, with the following formulas he gives the leaves together with the cooked rice, two at a time with each formula, to the eleven divine hosts.
As before, with the following formulas.

children.text: odanapiṇḍaṃ saṃvṛtya parṇapuṭe 'vadhāyottareṇa yajuṣā vṛkṣa āsajati ||
children.translated_text: Having wrapped up a lump of cooked rice, placed it in a leaf-cup, he hangs it on a tree with the following yajus.
At this point he should recite the Rudra formulas.
Or the first and last ones.

children.text: abhita etam agniṃ gāḥ sthāpayati yathaitā dhūmaḥ prāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: He stations cows around this fire so that the smoke reaches them.
He sprinkles them with perfumes by means of a handful of darbha grass, first the bull.
In the path of the cows, away from the fire, he worships the lord of the field.
The invocation is as in the rite for <s>Īśāna</s>.

children.text: caturṣu saptasu vā parṇeṣu nāmādeśaṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: On four or seven leaves he places the name-designation.
The cooked offering should be sacrificed quickly; the deity is eager.
He worships with the following two formulas.
He should feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with the sthālīpāka.
Those who are related by the same navel eat the portion for the lord of the field.
According as their family custom may be.
For the monthly śrāddha, in the latter fortnight, the times are as prescribed.

children.text: śucīn mantravato yonigotramantrāsambandhān ayugmāṃs tryavarān anarthāvekṣo bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: Without regard for material advantage, he should feed an odd number, at least three, who are pure, know the mantras, and are not connected by birth, gotra, or mantra.
With the following formulas he offers portions of the food.
The following are oblations of ghee.
Or this may be reversed.
He should touch everything with the following formulas.
Or prepared portions for each person.
Having made them touch with the following yajus formula...

children.text: bhuktavato 'nuvrajya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya dvaidhaṃ dakṣiṇāgrān darbhān saṃstīrya teṣūttarair apo dattvottarair dakṣiṇāpavargān piṇḍān dattvā pūrvavad uttarair apo dattvottarair upasthāyottarayodapātreṇa triḥ prasavyaṃ pariṣicya nyubjya pātrāṇy uttaraṃ yajur anavānaṃ tryavarārdhyam āvartayitvā prokṣya pātrāṇi dvandvam abhy udāhṛtya sarvataḥ samavadāyottareṇa yajuṣāśeṣasya grāsāvarārdhyaṃ prāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having accompanied him after he has eaten, and having circumambulated him clockwise, he spreads darbha grass in two portions with their tips to the south. On them, with the following formulas, he gives water; with the following formulas he gives the piṇḍas (ancestral rice-balls), ending toward the south; as before, with the following formulas he gives water. Having attended upon them with the following formulas, with the following water-vessel he sprinkles around three times counterclockwise, turns the vessels upside down, repeats the next yajus without taking breath, at least three times, sprinkles the vessels, raises them two by two, cuts off equally from all sides, and with the following yajus he should eat a mouthful, at least, of what remains.

children.text: yā māghyāḥ paurṇamāsyā upariṣṭād vyaṣṭakā tasyām aṣṭamī jyeṣṭhayā sampadyate tām ekāṣṭakety ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: The eighth day which falls together with the eldest lunar mansion after the full moon of <s>Māgha</s> is called the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>.
On its evening there is the preparatory rite.
He cooks a cake in four dishes.
Some say it is one of eight potsherds.
As in the full-moon rite, after the ājyabhāgas, he offers from the cake with his joined hands, using the following formula.

children.text: siddhaḥ śeṣas tam aṣṭadhā kṛtvā brāhmaṇebhya upaharati ||
children.translated_text: The remainder is ready; having divided it into eight parts, he presents it to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

children.text: śvobhūte darbheṇa gām upākaroti pitṛbhyas tvā juṣṭām upākaromīti ||
children.translated_text: On the following day he brings up a cow with darbha grass, saying, "I bring you up, acceptable to the Fathers."

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ pañcājyāhutīr hutvā tasyai vapāṃ śrapayitvopastīrṇābhighāritāṃ madhyamenāntamena vā palāśaparṇenottarayā juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Having silently offered five ghee oblations, cooked her omentum, spread it on a middle or end leaf of palāśa and sprinkled it with ghee, he offers it with the following formula.
He offers meat-rice with the following formulas.
He offers food made of flour with the following formula.
The following are ghee oblations.
From the sviṣṭakṛt onward the procedure is the same, up to the depositing of the piṇḍas.
Some teach that the depositing of the piṇḍas is to be done only on the <s>Anvaṣṭakā</s>.

children.text: athaitad aparaṃ dadhna evāñjalinā juhoti yayāpūpam ||
children.translated_text: Then, as an additional rite, he offers curds only, with joined hands, using the same formula with which he offered the cake.

children.text: ata eva yathārthaṃ māṃsaṃ śiṣṭvā śvobhūte 'nvaṣṭakām ||
children.translated_text: For the same reason, after leaving meat as required, on the following day he performs the <s>Anvaṣṭakā</s>.
Its procedure has been explained by the monthly śrāddha.
Having gone with a purpose, and having recited the following formulas, he should state the matter.

children.text: rathaṃ labdhvā yojayitvā prāñcam avasthāpyottarayā rathacakre abhimṛśati pakṣasī vā ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained a chariot, yoked it, and stationed it facing east, he touches the wheels of the chariot, or the two side-pieces, with the following formula.

children.text: uttareṇa yajuṣādhiruhyottarayā prācīm udīcīṃ vā diśam abhiprayāya yathārthaṃ yāyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having mounted it with the following yajus and set out with the following formula toward the east or the north, he should go as required.
He should mount a horse with the following formulas.
He mounts an elephant with the following formula.
When jolted by these two, he should touch the earth as before.

children.text: saṃvādam eṣyan savyena pāṇinā chatraṃ daṇḍaṃ cādatte ||
children.translated_text: When he is going to a conversation, he takes a parasol and a staff in his left hand.

children.text: dakṣiṇena phalīkaraṇamuṣṭim uttarayā hutvā gatvottarāṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: With his right hand, after offering a handful of parched grains with the following formula, he goes and recites the following one.
He should address an angry person with the following two formulas; the person becomes free from anger.

children.text: asaṃbhavepsuḥ pareṣāṃ sthūlāḍhārikājīvacūrṇāni kārayitvottarayā suptāyāḥ sambādha upavapet ||
children.translated_text: Desiring failure for others, he should have coarse śūlāḍhārikā and ājīva powders prepared and, with the following formula, strew them in the private parts of a sleeping woman.
For success he should wash with the urine of a brown animal.

children.text: siddhyarthe yad asya gṛhe paṇyaṃ syāt tata uttarayā juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: For success, from whatever merchandise there may be in his house, he should offer with the following formula.

children.text: yaṃ kāmayeta nāyaṃ mac chidyeteti jīvaviṣāṇe svaṃ mūtram ānīya suptam uttarābhyāṃ triḥ prasavyaṃ pariṣiñcet ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes of someone, "May this person not be separated from me," he should put his own urine into a living horn and sprinkle the sleeping person three times counterclockwise with the following two formulas.

children.text: yena pathā dāsakarmakarāḥ palāyeran tasminn iṇḍvāny upasamādhāyottarā āhutīr juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: On the path by which slaves and hired workers might flee, he should place iṇḍvā plants on the fire and offer the following oblations.

children.text: yady enaṃ vṛkṣāt phalam abhinipated vayo vābhivikṣiped avarṣatarkye vā bindur abhinipatet tad uttarair yathāliṅgaṃ prakṣālayīta ||
children.translated_text: If fruit should fall on him from a tree, or a bird should defecate on him, or in doubtful weather a drop should fall on him, he should wash it off with the following formulas, according to the sign.

children.text: āgārasthūṇāvirohaṇe madhuna upaveśane kuptvāṃ kapotapadadarśane 'mātyānāṃ śarīrareṣaṇe 'nyeṣu cādbhutotpāteṣv amāvāsyāyāṃ niśāyāṃ yatrāpāṃ na śṛṇuyāt tad agner upasamādhānādyājyabhāgānta uttarā āhutīr hutvā jayādi pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: When there is climbing on a house-post, sitting on honey, a kapota-foot mark on a vessel, marks of scraping on the bodies of ministers, and in other wondrous portents, on the night of the new moon, in a place where the sound of water is not heard, beginning with the placing of the fire and ending with the ājyabhāgas, he offers the following oblations and then proceeds to the jaya and the rest.

children.text: pariṣecanāntaṃ kṛtvābhimṛtebhya uttarayā dakṣiṇato 'śmānaṃ paridhiṃ dadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite down to the final sprinkling around, with the following formula he places a stone as a paridhi to the south for those who have been attacked.
